text: Design a high-performance n-i-p perovskite solar cell with a target PCE above 25%. I have not yet selected the HTL or ETL. Constraints: perovskite bandgap around 1.55 eV, HTL work function in the range 5.1-5.3 eV, ETL work function in the range 4.0-4.3 eV, high electron and hole mobilities, and good energetic alignment with the perovskite. Please propose suitable HTL/ETL materials and a complete device architecture that satisfies these constraints. Use the literature to justify the material choices, retrieve relevant material properties, predict the expected PCE, and identify which design parameters are most important for further improvement.

ASK pdb: Query the Perovskite Database for experimental n-i-p perovskite solar cells with a perovskite bandgap between 1.50 and 1.60 eV achieving PCE > 24%. What are the top ETL and HTL materials used in these high-efficiency devices? Report the most common ETL/HTL combinations, typical layer configurations, and their average/maximum Voc, Jsc, FF, and PCE.
ASK literature: Find literature passages and DOIs for high-performance n-i-p perovskite solar cells (PCE > 24-25%) with bandgap ~1.55 eV. Specifically, report material properties and energetic alignment for candidate ETLs with work function/conduction band around 4.0-4.3 eV (such as SnO2 or TiO2) and HTLs with work function/HOMO around 5.1-5.3 eV (such as Spiro-OMeTAD, PTAA). Include values for band edges/work functions, electron/hole mobilities, and verbatim quotes justifying why these materials provide good alignment and high efficiency.
ASK design: Design and simulate in SCAPS-1D an n-i-p perovskite solar cell targeting >25% PCE with a 1.55 eV perovskite absorber. Use an ETL with conduction band/work function around 4.0-4.3 eV (e.g., SnO2) and an HTL with HOMO/work function around 5.1-5.3 eV (e.g., Spiro-OMeTAD or PTAA). Specify the layer stack (thicknesses, carrier concentrations, mobilities, defect densities, band alignment) and run the simulation. Return the simulated Voc, Jsc, FF, and PCE along with the complete device structure.
ASK ml: Predict the expected PCE with uncertainty for an n-i-p perovskite solar cell having a 1.55 eV bandgap perovskite absorber (e.g. FA-rich / mixed-cation perovskite), SnO2 ETL, and Spiro-OMeTAD or PTAA HTL. Compute SHAP values / feature importance to identify which design parameters (e.g., thickness, mobility, defect density, bandgap, contact work functions) are most influential for achieving and exceeding 25% PCE, and provide optimization recommendations.
